title: Data & transactions
subtitle: Store data and define transaction boundaries with Spring Data JPA.
description: Map entities to tables, create repositories, and group related database operations in transactions. Write schema migrations and inspect SQL to find N+1 queries.

lessons.title: Entity, ID & repository
lessons.summary: JPA maps Java objects to relational tables. Spring Data creates repository implementations from interfaces.
objectives: Map an entity and generated primary key.
Keep persistence entities separate from API DTOs.
keyPoints: Entity and Id define an entity and its primary key.
JPA entities need a no-argument constructor; protected is sufficient.
Use explicit DTOs so persistence changes do not alter the public API.
practice: Map Order to orders and add a repository query by status.
The application persists orders and can retrieve them by status.

exercises.prompt: Make Order a JPA entity with an IDENTITY-generated primary key and a protected no-argument constructor.
exercises.explanation: Table(name = "orders") avoids the SQL keyword order. A protected constructor satisfies JPA without inviting ordinary callers to create an empty entity.

exercises.prompt: Complete the derived query method name to query WHERE status = ?.
exercises.hint: Start with findBy and add the property name.
exercises.explanation: Spring Data derives the condition from findByStatus and other supported query prefixes.

exercises.prompt: Why avoid returning an entity directly from an API?
options: Internal fields may leak and schema changes may alter the public contract.
JSON serialization may trigger lazy loading and extra queries.
Entities cannot be serialized to JSON at all.
Spring forbids it and refuses to start.
exercises.explanation: Map entities to DTOs explicitly to control the API contract and the data loaded for a response.

lessons.title: Local transaction boundaries
lessons.summary: Transactional groups database changes into a unit that commits or rolls back according to its rollback rules.
objectives: Recognize self-invocation that bypasses a proxy.
keyPoints: RuntimeException and Error trigger rollback by default.
Checked exceptions require an explicit rollback rule when rollback is intended.
Calls through this do not pass through the Spring transaction proxy.
practice: Load an order and confirm it in one transaction.
Dirty checking writes the state change on commit, and a failed operation does not leave partial data.

exercises.prompt: A Transactional method throws a checked IOException. What happens under the default rollback rules?
options: The transaction commits; checked exceptions do not trigger rollback by default.
exercises.explanation: Use rollbackFor when a checked exception should roll back, or use an appropriate unchecked domain exception.

exercises.prompt: placeAll has no transaction annotation and calls this.place(), which has Transactional. Does that call start a transaction?
options: No. Self-invocation bypasses the Spring transaction proxy.
Yes. The annotation applies regardless of how the call arrives.
Yes, but only for public methods.
exercises.explanation: Annotate the externally called method or move place into another injected bean so the call passes through its proxy.

exercises.prompt: Make confirm transactional, load the order, call order.confirm(), and let dirty checking save the change.
checks: Handle a missing order with orElseThrow
exercises.explanation: A managed entity is tracked by the persistence context. Its changes are flushed when the transaction commits.

lessons.title: Schema migration
lessons.summary: Record schema changes as ordered, versioned scripts so databases can be upgraded consistently.
objectives: Plan compatible changes to existing data.
keyPoints: Flyway records applied versions and checksums.
Use validate or none when migrations own schema changes.
Add nullable data first, backfill it, and tighten constraints after the application is ready.
practice: Add order status through a versioned migration and test both an empty and an existing database.
The migration works without losing data or breaking the previous application version.

exercises.prompt: Name the Flyway version 2 SQL migration with description add_order_status.
exercises.hint: Use V, the version, two underscores, the description, and .sql.
exercises.explanation: V2__add_order_status.sql follows Flyway naming. There are two underscores before the description.

exercises.prompt: Order the safe steps for adding a required status column to an existing table.
items: Backfill old rows with UPDATE orders SET status = 'NEW'.
Release an application version that always fills status for new rows.
Add NOT NULL and a default in a later migration.
exercises.explanation: Separate the schema and application changes so old and new versions can coexist during rollout.

exercises.prompt: Which ddl-auto value fits a schema managed by Flyway?
exercises.explanation: Let Flyway apply schema changes. validate checks entity mappings without silently changing the database.

lessons.title: Relationships & query performance
lessons.summary: Object relationships can trigger additional SQL. Inspect the queries and load only the data each use case needs.
objectives: Load a needed relationship with JOIN FETCH.
keyPoints: Loading a list and then each item collection may produce N+1 queries.
JOIN FETCH or EntityGraph can load the relationship explicitly.
For paginated collections, consider fetching IDs first and relationships in a second query.
practice: Inspect SQL for an order list and replace N+1 loading with an explicit fetch query.
The relevant use case loads its needed items without one query per order.

exercises.prompt: Loading 20 orders and then each item collection produces 21 queries. What is this called?
exercises.explanation: One query loads orders and 20 additional queries load their items. The query count grows with the result size.

exercises.prompt: Write an @Query method that loads orders and their items in one query using JOIN FETCH.
checks: Use join fetch o.items in JPQL
exercises.explanation: JOIN FETCH loads the requested relationship in the query. EntityGraph is another option for declaring the needed fetch plan.
